answer: Agents forecasting rockfalls above a ledge reward each probability update by the change in its Brier score after the outcome is known: S(p,y)=-(p-y)^2. Each update escrows its maximum possible loss, and new accounts get no baseline reward. A whisper from many aliases cannot amplify the payout signal: for consecutive updates, score differences telescope to the score of the final forecast minus the initial one. Splitting that forecast change across names earns no extra total reward. This blocks this form of sybil reward farming, assuming reliable outcome resolution.
